policies.name: Medical Nutrition Therapy (MNT) Act (H.R. 6199 / S. 3934)
policies.status: Introduced in Committee (119th Congress ends Jan 3, 2027)
policies.summary: H.R. 6199 (introduced Nov 20, 2025 by Rep. Robin Kelly, D-IL) and S. 3934 (introduced Feb 26, 2026 by Sens. Collins & Peters; cosponsored by Sens. Marshall, Booker, Klobuchar, Warner) expand Medicare Part B MNT beyond diabetes and renal disease to include obesity, prediabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, cancer, CVD, HIV/AIDS, GI/celiac disease, malnutrition, and eating disorders. Also authorizes NPs, PAs, CNSs, and psychologists to refer.
policies.so_what: Unlikely to pass before the 119th Congress adjourns on Jan 3, 2027 due to lack of CBO score/committee action; expect reintroduction in early 2027 (120th Congress).
spicerack_recommendations: Enroll the Spicerack PLLC and each individual RD in Medicare now to build billing workflows and capture existing Medicare MNT revenue for diabetes and renal patients.
Build a direct local advocacy relationship with Rep. Robin Kelly's office (IL-02, bill sponsor) and the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics advocacy team.
Prepare administrative workflows for referral documentation and expanded ICD-10 diagnosis coding ahead of 120th Congress reintroduction in January 2027.

policies.name: Dietitian Licensure Compact
policies.summary: Interstate compact allowing RDs/RDNs with an unencumbered license in a member home state to practice across member states via a 'compact privilege' without separate individual licenses. Enacted in 19 states across 2024-2026 (AL, NE, TN, AR, IA, KS, MS, MT, ND, OH, OK, RI, SD, UT, WI, GA, KY, MO, WA). Activation threshold (7 states) met; 12-24 month implementation means privileges are expected in 2027. Illinois has not introduced a bill yet.
policies.so_what: No compact privileges are issued yet, and Illinois is not yet a member state. Furthermore, the compact only covers individual RD licensure—not PLLC corporate entity qualification.
spicerack_recommendations: Limit near-term state expansion to non-licensure or low-barrier states until compact privileges officially issue in 2027.
Verify foreign entity qualification and professional ownership rules in each target state to confirm an Illinois-licensed PLLC can legally operate there.
Build a state-by-state Practice Act compliance guide for Spicerack RDs, as practitioners remain legally responsible for obeying the remote state's scope of practice.
Recruit RDs residing in the 19 enacted compact member states so they can immediately leverage multi-state compact privileges once issued in 2027, and advocate for an Illinois compact bill.

policies.name: Medicare Telehealth Policy (CAA 2026 / H.R. 7148)
policies.summary: The Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2026 (H.R. 7148, signed Feb 2026) extended Medicare telehealth flexibilities through December 31, 2027 and retroactively covered the post-Jan 30, 2026 lapse. While RDs are permanently eligible distant-site practitioners and MNT codes are permanent on the Medicare Telehealth List, the waiver allowing patients to receive telehealth at home (SSA § 1834(m) / 42 C.F.R. § 410.78) expires Dec 31, 2027.
policies.so_what: Home-based Medicare MNT telehealth is secure through 2027, but if Congress fails to pass an extension or permanent law by Dec 31, 2027, beneficiaries would have to travel to rural qualifying originating sites.
spicerack_recommendations: Diversify Spicerack's payer mix with commercial payers and value-based B2B contracts now so post-2027 revenue is not solely dependent on Congressional Medicare extensions.
Maintain strict intake and clinical documentation of patient physical location at every visit to satisfy both state telehealth laws and potential post-2027 Medicare originating-site audits.
Remember that federal Medicare telehealth waivers do not override state-level licensure or state telehealth practice standards.

policies.name: CMS ACCESS Model
policies.summary: 10-year voluntary CMMI model supporting virtual and asynchronous technology-enabled chronic care for Original Medicare. Launched July 2026 with 150 organizations; expanded Sept 15, 2026 to add heart failure, COPD, SUD, and tobacco cessation alongside eCKM (obesity, prediabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia) and CKM (diabetes, CKD, ASCVD). Pays Outcome-Aligned Payments of $180-$360 in Year 1 per patient/track and $90-$210 for follow-on care through Dec 31, 2027.
policies.so_what: Unlike traditional Medicare MNT, ACCESS pays directly for obesity, prediabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidemia management under the eCKM track, and major commercial payers (CVS, Humana, UHC, Cigna, BSCA) pledged aligned options.
spicerack_recommendations: Complete the CMS ACCESS rolling interest form and review the participation agreement specifically targeting the eCKM (obesity, prediabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia) and CKM tracks.
Use the ACCESS Outcome-Aligned Payment bands ($180-$360 Year 1; $90-$210 follow-on care) to build Spicerack's internal financial and unit-economics models.
Leverage ACCESS to get reimbursed for Original Medicare obesity and prediabetes patients that standard Part B MNT currently excludes.

policies.name: CMS LEAD Model
policies.summary: Long-term Enhanced ACO Design (LEAD) is CMS's 10-year successor to ACO REACH (Jan 1, 2027 - Dec 31, 2036) with Global Risk (100% shared savings/losses) and Professional Risk (up to 50%) tracks plus primary/total care capitation. Participating ACOs must have at least 5,000 aligned Original Medicare beneficiaries.
policies.so_what: Because LEAD ACOs bear heavy downside risk and receive capitated cash flows, they can pay Spicerack directly for preventive nutrition services (like non-diabetic obesity care) that Fee-For-Service Medicare denies.
spicerack_recommendations: Monitor CMS for the published list of accepted LEAD ACOs and filter for hospital networks, physician groups, and FQHCs operating in Illinois and Spicerack's target expansion states.
Pitch LEAD ACOs a predictable per-member-per-month (PMPM) or case-rate nutrition program so ACOs can budget fixed preventive care expenses against their downside risk.
Highlight Spicerack's ability to manage non-diabetic obesity and cardiometabolic risk for the ACO's 5,000+ aligned Original Medicare beneficiaries.

policies.name: CMS BALANCE Model
policies.impact_area: Payment Model, Pharma B2B Partnerships, GLP-1 Wrap-Around
policies.summary: Announced Dec 23, 2025 under SSA § 1115A, BALANCE lowers GLP-1 net prices and caps out-of-pocket costs across Medicare Part D and Medicaid while mandating that participating pharmaceutical manufacturers provide or support evidence-based lifestyle, fitness, and nutrition counseling. State Medicaid agencies can join from May 2026 through Jan 1, 2027 (Illinois Medicaid participation is not yet confirmed).
policies.so_what: Spicerack cannot apply to CMS as a standalone participant to bill BALANCE directly; revenue depends entirely on B2B vendor partnerships with participating GLP-1 manufacturers.
spicerack_recommendations: Submit vendor partnership proposals directly through Novo Nordisk's Digital Partnerships portal and Eli Lilly's Supplier Development portal to serve as their virtual RD lifestyle wrap-around provider.
Do not spend administrative resources attempting to apply directly to CMS as a standalone billing provider for BALANCE.
Track whether the Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (Medicaid) submits a State RFA prior to the January 1, 2027 deadline.
